speaker: Doctor
text:
Welcome to my office. I see you are presenting with fatigue, severe itching, and abnormal liver function tests; to begin our assessment, have you noticed any jaundice, dark urine, or pale stools recently?

REQUEST TEST: Liver_Function_Panel (Complete)
REQUEST TEST: Viral_Hepatitis_Serology (A, B, C)
REQUEST TEST: Autoimmune_Panel (ANA, ASMA, AMA)

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Liver Function Tests: Hemoglobin 11.5 g/dL, Bilirubin_Total 1.5 mg/dL, Bilirubin_Direct 0.9 mg/dL, Alkaline_Phosphatase 460 U/L, AST 75 U/L, ALT 78 U/L. Autoimmune Panel: Anti-Nuclear_Antibody Negative, Antimitochondrial_Antibodies Negative. (Note: Viral_Hepatitis_Serology results were not included in the provided data.)

speaker: Doctor
text: The labs show a significant cholestatic pattern with markedly elevated alkaline phosphatase (460 U/L) and mild hyperbilirubinemia, but your autoimmune and viral hepatitis screens are negative. Did you recently experience any fever, night sweats, or unintentional weight loss?

speaker: Patient
text: 32-year-old male. The patient reports a 2-month history of increasing generalized fatigue and severe pruritus. He has known hypertension and was diagnosed with ulcerative colitis 5 years ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and inconsistent condom use.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given your history of ulcerative colitis and these specific lab results, could you confirm if you have been diagnosed with Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis (PSC) in the past? Additionally, have you noticed any new abdominal pain or a change in bowel habits recently?

REQUEST IMAGES: MRCP (Magnetic Resonance Cholangiopancreatography)

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Generalized fatigue and severe pruritus. I also have Scleral icterus, Multiple scratch marks on trunk and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis (PSC). The combination of elevated alkaline phosphatase, scleral icterus, a history of ulcerative colitis, and negative autoimmune/viral screens is classic for PSC. I have requested the MRCP images to confirm the characteristic "beads on a string" appearance of the biliary tree.
